title: How are you making art assets?
author: mizerr
selftext:
There's no question coding agents and option are accelerating at incredible speeds. It seems at this time for ai game dev specifically, art is the choke point for producing quality games. I have not found excellent workflows for assets, especially not 3d. From my experience, 3d assets need manual work just to get them to game-ready, and then they are hand placed and maps hand built.

  
I'm curious how others are approaching art and how automated workflows have been achieved.

comments.author: runner_1
comments.body:
I too am interested in this question.  
  
I have been creating my own workflows using ComfyUI to generate sprite sheets but still spinning my wheels on it a bit. I've also experimented a bit with ludo ai with some positive results but its a bit cost ineffective.

replies.author: megapiano
replies.body: Can you say more about Ludo AI? I'm considering using it. Does it work well? Are the spritesheet animations okay? Any input you have about it I would appreciate.

replies.author: runner_1
replies.body:
I think it works well enough for you to take a deeper dive on it. The main issue I have is the costs. You get a fixed amount of credits each month and it's far too easy to burn through them when everything takes several fine tuning iterations.

  
Here's a man on a horse I generated and animated just now. My animated prompt was "Galloping". Ludo made him spin around.

https://i.redd.it/0qxac9dnyxhg1.gif

  
Generating audio for the sprite animations seems decent but I have not used it much yet.

comments.author: estebansaa
comments.body: Just posted something similar in another group, Im able to generate tiles, but is challenging to get consistent results.  Im not interested in services or apis offering this as a servic, I need to do it locally for my projects.

comments.author: Microtom_
comments.body: I'm making my 2d pixel art with nano banana pro. Later I might train a model from what I accumulated.

replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body: Im working on a pixel art editor that will hopefully allow AI plugin so you generate and edit all in one spot if you do end up getting a model trained definitely keep me in mind I would love to plug it in to the editor, as I haven't even thought of starting that part as I am no where close to that point

comments.author: RealAstropulse
comments.body: 3d ai game assets still seem pretty far in the stone ages. I'd wait for that tech to mature more. 2d ai gen art is just recently getting to where it can be useful for most games.

comments.author: OldGoldCode
comments.body: I wrote a custom pipeline that can convert glb meshes into other formats and clean them up, I get the original formats from a fork of Trellis.

comments.author: Wobstep
comments.body:
I developed a decent pace for making 2d pixel art before image gen was good. I end up drawing a few basic sprites as a skeleton and then ask the agent to make placeholders for things to expand the content. 

For example, I'll say "need the minimum amount of sprite variation to be able to make 10,000 unique character combinations. If I make the sprites in grey scale and ask the agent to make as much variety with the image it can, it will give me a list of like 60 or so sprites to make and then create the folders to place them in with readme checklists. 

It will reuse sprites I made for ui for placeholders and sometimes the results are spot on. Without even generating art or spending too much time drawing, I have a good workflow of making my art repeatable so ai can fill in the gaps. 

I found my own personal sweet spot using the cursor and godot. Obsidian for documents then pixelorama for art. Maybe it already exists but I'm waiting for a good solution for pixel art and this is the closest I have got so far to generative pixel art that looks the way I want it to.

comments.author: chunky_lover92
comments.body: text to image and inpainting with krita diffusions then hunyuan3d for image to mesh.  I'm mostly getting pretty far with premade assets though.

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: Gemini for a outline then I make it look good by hand I stopped trying to get game ready assets so I only trust AI to generate me a outline or a rough draft with the thought of throwing it in a editor as soon as it's done generating

comments.author: beelllllll
comments.body: I built autosprite io for this

comments.author: pikqwe
comments.body: I used couple ais to build in house use tool to generate pixel art and various other features like slicing, atlas creation, sprite animation, different poses etc etc. And I can add any API key and keep producing.

comments.author: HerbertGoon
comments.body: I have the game procedurally generate everything to look as good as possible.

comments.author: 88chilly
comments.body: What I’m seeing is basically: AI for concepts with  rough meshes, then lots of manual cleanup to make things game-ready. Modular kits and procedural tools help way more than pure text-to-3D. Fully automated 3D pipelines still feel not there yet.

comments.author: Elegant_Gas_740
comments.body:
Art is still the bottleneck because AI can generate assets but not reliably make them game ready clean topology, UVs, proper scale, LODs, collisions.
Most people use AI for concept and rough models, then do manual cleanup in Blender / Unity / Unreal.

comments.author: RelapseCatAddict
comments.body: I use a mixture of ChatGPT,canva,Gemini , and pixel lab to make my images

comments.author: MakkoMakkerton
comments.body: From many conversations with devs from different backgrounds 3d will be the hardest because AI is not there yet in terms of robustness. Sure you can make a 3d model with AI, but its not as easy as it is with 2d assets and what we currently have. AI will catch up, but just creating a 3d model dosnt mean it will work in the game or even adjust properly to the engine you want to use it in. Unity and Unreal are different and moving assets made in one to the other is actually a bit of a headache. Would be curious to see who can streamline this process

comments.author: Apache_Choppah_6969
comments.body: I tried a few 3d tools but they're all extremely bad, nothing was able to produce anything near-game-ready and most hallucinate to the moon and back
